To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the combination of an antibody against BudR with a second antibody, and the use of side scatter instead of fluorescence, allows a more precise identification of BudR+cells.

(i) the combination of anti-BudR and anti-IgGH+L antibodies allows the analysis of cell cycle and cellular markers; (ii) side scatter allows a better discrimination between BudR- and BudR+ cells; (iii) the combination of these techniques allows a better analysis of low incorporating cells; (iv) this methodology allows the analysis of specific subpopulations of cells in the cell cycle; (v) this approach is useful in the analysis of cell death and proliferation
the use of an IgGH+IgGL anti-BudR antibody and side scatter, rather than PI fluorescence, for the analysis of DNA synthesis allows a better discrimination and collection of the BudR+ population.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of monoclonal antibodies to BrdUr in flow cytometry to study the cell cycle and its correlation with cellular markers.
the development and application of flow cytometric methodologies to analyse cell cycle in different experimental models.
the development of new methodologies for the analysis of cell cycle in the presence of BudR.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of anti-BudR antibodies in conjunction with a right angle light scatter signal is a useful tool for the analysis of cell cycle distribution in a four parameter flow cytometer.
the use of the anti-BudR antibody and the right angle light scatter is an efficient and reliable methodology to perform dynamic cell cycle analysis.
this methodology allows the analysis of a wide range of cells, from low to high incorporation rates, in a very simple and rapid manner.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of side scatter and anti-BudR antibodies allows a better discrimination between BudR+ and BudR- cells.
the combination of anti-BudR and side scatter allows us to discriminate between cells with different DNA contents, and also to correlate this parameter to other cellular characteristics.
we have developed a new methodology for the detection and characterization of cells in the cell cycle.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of anti-BrdU antibodies in conjunction with side scatter allows a better discrimination between BudR+ and BudR- cells and the correlation between cell cycle and other cellular markers.
the use of side-scatter instead of propidum iodide fluorescence in the analysis of BrdU/DNA cells allows for better discrimination of the BrdU+ cells and a better correlation with other cell markers.
, in the absence of a fluorescent signal, side scatter can be used to identify cells with different DNA content.
